9.0.s.en: 1. The queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon and her honoring of him

9.0.0.en: 1 And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart. 2 And Solomon told her all her questions: and there was nothing hid from Solomon which he told her not. 3 And when the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built, 4 And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel; his cupbearers also, and their apparel; and his burnt offerings that he offered up in the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her. 5 And she said to the king, “It was a true report which I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom: 6 Howbeit I believed not their words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me: for thou exceedest the fame that I heard. 7 Happy are thy men, and happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and hear thy wisdom. 8 Blessed be the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for the LORD thy God: because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice.” 9 And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices great abundance, and precious stones: neither was there any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave king Solomon. 10 And the servants also of Huram, and the servants of Solomon, which brought gold from Ophir, brought algum trees and precious stones. 11 And the king made of the algum trees terraces to the house of the LORD, and to the king's palace, and harps and psalteries for singers: and there were none such seen before in the land of Judah. 12 And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which she had brought unto the king. So she turned, and went away to her own land, she and her servants.

9.0.1.en: This story is told in detail in the First Book of Kings, and the Lord Christ Himself referred to it (Mt 12:42). The following is noticeable in this story: 1. The meeting of the queen of Sheba with Solomon is considered a call addressed to every person to meet One who is greater than Solomon, namely the Wisdom of God Himself, the Creator of Solomon and the One who gave him wisdom. The Lord Christ reproached the Jews who did not receive Him, while the queen of Sheba, who was of the Gentiles, came to Solomon to hear him.

9.1.0.en: What the queen of Sheba enjoyed in her meeting with Solomon cannot be compared with what we enjoy in our meeting and fellowship with the Lord of Solomon and his Savior. 2. Solomon did not invite the queen of Sheba to visit him, nor did she need to investigate the facts about Solomon, but she hurried to see with her own eyes [6]. His glory drew her.

9.1.1.en: The person of Solomon attracted many, even kings, and in this he differs from many kings who gained worldwide fame: on the one hand, he did not gain his fame by wars and violence, but by the spirit of wisdom together with peace. In his days as king, his kingdom extended for forty years, and we do not hear that he fought any battle with any of the nations or peoples. On the other hand, his relationship with the kings and peoples carried mutual respect, for he exchanged precious gifts with the queen of Sheba, and generously.

9.2.0.en: When she met him she realized that what she touched was far greater than what she had heard about him. So also when our Christ reveals His glory in us, His fragrant aroma in us bears witness for us, and we are ready to answer everyone who asks us a reason of the hope that is in us (1 Pet 3:15). 3. Hiram, king of Tyre, offered Solomon much gold and timber and other building materials, and also men skilled in building and workmen, but he did not go to Solomon to become a disciple of his wisdom. But the queen of Sheba came to him and listened to his wisdom. 4. The queen of Sheba met Solomon, and her soul rejoiced, a reference to the Lord Christ, the fountain of joy for everyone who meets Him. 5. She blessed those who stand before him continually, because they see his face and hear his wisdom. 6. She highlighted his authority over all the kings from the river to the land of the Philistines [26]. Truly, those who honor God, He honors (1 Sam 2:30). Solomon honored God greatly, whether by building the Temple, adorning it and dedicating it, or by praising Him and thanking Him, or by consecrating what God gave him of wisdom and riches for the sake of the Kingdom of God and the service of His people. 7. The queen of Sheba bore many troubles and great expense to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and yet she considered that, having heard his wisdom, she was rewarded with much. The wisdom of Solomon was a symbol of the Hypostasis of Wisdom, our Lord Jesus, who draws souls and brings them into the bosom of the Father. 8. Solomon knew how to kindle the gift that was given to him freely, and he offered it freely to others. If any gifts were offered to him, they did not occupy him; what occupied him was that all should enjoy the wisdom of God. 9. What caught the attention of the queen of Sheba was the good management of Solomon's household, of those who worked with him and of his servants. Some see that Solomon, in his speaking about wisdom or the management of the affairs of worship and so on, drew the heart of the queen of Sheba to the Lord Christ, the only sacrifice of atonement, who is able to complete salvation for all who come from among men. 10. The influence of Solomon by his wisdom in the Lord was not only on his servants who served him, but also on their sons, for they took pride in being called “the children of Solomon's servants” (Ezra 2:55; Neh 7:57). 11. The queen of Sheba presented a living example of sincere love, for she praised God for His work with the people of Israel through King Solomon [8].

9.2.1.en: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart. [1]

9.2.2.en: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon through the merchants who pass by Sheba with their ships. Here the queen of Sheba presents a living picture of the true believer from many aspects: 1. The queen did not stop at hearing about Solomon, but moved to meet him and to prove him, not in doubt of what she had heard, otherwise she would not have come bearing these precious gifts, but she came to enjoy meeting him. In this she is a symbol of the Magi who, when they saw the star, moved with their gifts toward Jerusalem to meet the One born King of the Jews and to worship Him.

9.2.3.en: In contrast to this, when King Herod gathered the chief priests and scribes of the people together (Mt 2:4) and asked them where Christ should be born, they offered him the prophecy, but did not move to meet the Christ who was born.

9.2.4.en: v They prepared gifts for the King that He might be honored by them, so that they might enter into His presence with offerings when they beheld Him.

9.2.5.en: When they took care to prepare the offerings, the Truth arose to teach them what they must do.

9.2.6.en: They opened their treasures and brought gold, because He is the great King, and they took myrrh, because He would become one slain.

9.2.7.en: Frankincense serves to honor Him, because He is also God: they brought spices and myrrh and gold to be offered to Him.

9.2.8.en: They carried the treasures of their fathers with joy, to offer their offerings to the great King...

9.2.9.en: They became preachers while walking on the way, proclaiming that the King has dawned upon the whole world...

9.2.10.en: Wherever they journeyed and wherever they halted, they told His story (saying): Our way is directed toward a mighty One born in Judea.

9.2.11.en: On their way His teaching shone forth, and at their appointed times their words were heard.

9.2.12.en: In every place where they halted they sowed the glad tidings, and when they departed they recounted the news of His birth.

9.2.13.en: Their preaching spread over the miles of the road, and in its stages those tidings were chanted[1].

9.2.14.en: St. Jacob of Serugh The queen told him all that was in her heart, and he told her all that she wanted to know [2]. This relationship represents the relationship of the soul with her Christ. On her part she reveals what is in her depths, and her Christ on His part tells her His divine secrets which she longs to know.

9.2.15.en: It is fitting for the believer to open his heart before his Savior, and to enter with Him into an open dialogue.

9.3.0.en: And Solomon told her all her questions.

9.3.1.en: And there was nothing hid from Solomon which he told her not. [2]

9.3.2.en: When the believer opens his heart for frank speech with his Savior, as the queen of Sheba did with Solomon, the Lord of glory opens the treasures of His secrets and hides nothing from him.

9.3.3.en: v The Son of God was called thus (the Messenger of the great counsel) because of the things that He taught, especially since He declared the Father to men, saying: “I have manifested thy name unto the men” (Jn 17:6)... He declared His name by words and works[2].

9.4.0.en: St. John Chrysostom v There is no knowledge without faith, and no faith without knowledge... The Son is the true Teacher about the Father; we believe in the Son in order to know the Father, with whom the Son also is. Again, in order to know the Father we must believe in the Son, for He is the Son of the Father. The knowledge of the Father and the Son, in the manner of the true Gnostic, is the attaining of truth by means of truth... Truly, few are those who believe and know[3].

9.5.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria v The divine Word was sent as a physician for sinners, and as a teacher of the divine mysteries to those who are pure and without sin[4].

9.6.0.en: Origen v A great scribe came down from heaven and became a teacher of the world. The whole world was enlightened by his teaching, lest anyone should desire any more the perishing possessions[5].

9.7.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh v Come, beloved, turn to the precious counsel which the Apostle offers you, for he says: [As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith]. In this simple and assured faith it is fitting for us to remain firmly rooted in Him, so that He Himself may open to the believers hidden in Him, as the same Apostle says: [In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge]. And He has not hidden them from anyone that they should reject them, but to stir up in them a longing for the treasured things[6].

9.8.0.en: And when the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built [3]

9.9.0.en: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel; his cupbearers also, and their apparel; and his burnt offerings that he offered up in the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her. [4]

9.9.1.en: The report of her visit to him reveals to us not only the greatness of Solomon's palace, but also the life that went on in the palace, from the food of his table and the sitting of his servants to the conduct of his ministers, even their apparel.

9.9.2.en: Most likely, as a Gentile, she was not taken to the house of the Lord, but she also knew of the burnt offerings which he offered through the priests.

9.9.3.en: The queen could not record her feelings about his life in his palace and his love and giving for the house of the Lord, but it was said: “There was no more spirit in her.”

9.9.4.en: What she saw and heard and touched was only a shadow, as happened with the Apostle Paul, who heard unspeakable words (2 Cor 12:4).

9.9.5.en: The queen realized that Solomon, his household and those who worked with him were the happiest people she had seen on the face of the earth! Here we recall what St. John Chrysostom wrote, that the Christian is the happiest person on earth.

9.9.6.en: The Holy Bible does not indicate whether the queen of Sheba visited the Temple, as it was the greatest thing Solomon built in the capital, yet his concern that his wife, the daughter of Pharaoh, should not dwell in the house of David suggests that he did not give the queen of Sheba the opportunity to visit the holy house of the Lord.

9.10.0.en: And she said to the king, It was a true report which I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom! [5]

9.11.0.en: Howbeit I believed not their words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me.

9.11.1.en: Thou exceedest the fame that I heard. [6]

9.11.2.en: How great is the difference between what the queen heard about the wisdom of Solomon and what she touched herself when she met him.

9.11.3.en: Truly, when the people came into touch with the wisdom of Solomon, they glorified the Lord, the Giver of wisdom.

9.11.4.en: v Then all the people of the house of Israel shouted to glorify the Lord who gave him wisdom.

9.11.5.en: Blessed is the Lord who keeps His love for His servant David, and raised up after him his son and filled him with wisdom...

9.11.6.en: May the throne of King Solomon be great over Israel, and may his fame spread among the princes and the peoples of the earth.

9.12.0.en: Let the queen of Sheba go and inquire about his wisdom (1 Kgs 10), and meet him with the perfumes of every fragrance[7].

9.13.0.en: Happy are thy men, and happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and hear thy wisdom. [7]

9.13.1.en: The queen of Sheba felt that her tongue was unable to express anything concerning Solomon himself, so she did not bless him, but blessed his men who worked with him and heard him. Perhaps she felt that he was too great for her to bless him, so she blessed those who meet him and enjoy him.

9.13.2.en: This is what the Lord Christ declared to those who clung to Him and saw Him and touched Him, saying to them: “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see” (Lk 10:23).

9.14.0.en: Blessed be the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for the LORD thy God.

9.14.1.en: Because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever.

9.14.2.en: Therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice. [8]

9.14.3.en: The queen of Sheba perceived God's love for His people, in that He made Solomon king over them to do judgment and justice (or righteousness), yet Solomon afterward burdened them with his demands in order to spend on his projects and constructions. But the Lord Christ, having reigned over humanity, gave Himself for the salvation of the world, and granted them His righteousness as righteousness for them.

9.14.4.en: v Christ is the goodness which the people were awaiting[8].

9.14.5.en: Origen v We who have Christ, the source of all necessities, dwelling in the heart, have been enriched at once in every kind of virtue, and have an abundance of steadfast spiritual gifts.

9.14.6.en: St. Cyril the Great v What does it mean: [And of his fulness have all we received] (Jn 1:16)?...

9.14.7.en: He says that He does not possess the gift by participation, but He Himself is the fountain of Himself and the origin of all goodness, Life itself, Light itself, Truth itself; He does not keep the riches of His goodness shut up within Himself, but overflows with it upon others, and after this overflowing He remains in His fulness, not diminished as He supplies others, but always overflowing, and giving to others that they may share His blessings, while He remains in His perfection as He is.

9.14.8.en: What I possess is by participation (that is, I receive it from another); I have a small share of the whole, like a poor drop of water compared with an infinite deep or a boundless sea. And even this illustration cannot express completely what we are trying to say...

9.15.0.en: Let us suppose there is a source of fire, and from this source tens of thousands of lamps are kindled... Does not the fire remain as it is in its fullness even after it has given of what is its to such a number? It is clear to every person that it is so[9].

9.16.0.en: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices great abundance, and precious stones: neither was there any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave king Solomon. [9]

9.16.1.en: The presenting of gifts to Solomon by the queen of Sheba, the Gentile, was a symbol of what the foreign Magi would do at the birth of the Lord Christ, the wonderful King, when they presented gifts to Him.

9.17.0.en: And the servants also of Huram, and the servants of Solomon, which brought gold from Ophir, brought algum trees and precious stones. [10]

9.18.0.en: And the king made of the algum trees terraces to the house of the LORD, and to the king's palace, and harps and psalteries for singers: and there were none such seen before in the land of Judah. [11]

9.19.0.en: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which she had brought unto the king.

9.19.1.en: So she turned, and went away to her own land, she and her servants. [12]

9.20.s.en: 2. The greatness of Solomon's court and his wealth

9.20.0.en: 13 Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold; 14 Beside that which chapmen and merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon. 15 And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one target. 16 And three hundred shields made he of beaten gold: three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon. 17 Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold. 18 And there were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and stays on each side of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays: 19 And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps. There was not the like made in any kingdom. 20 And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: none were of silver; it was not any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon. 21 For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks. 22 And king Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom. 23 And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that God had put in his heart. 24 And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year. 25 And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; whom he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem. 26 And he reigned over all the kings from the river even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt. 27 And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the low plains in abundance. 28 And they brought unto Solomon horses out of Egypt, and out of all lands.

9.20.1.en: Since God, who is all-rich in wealth, glory, power and wisdom, was with Solomon, He poured out of what is His upon His beloved. History does not mention a king with the wealth and glory of Solomon, together with his wisdom and his ability to create an atmosphere of peace with the nations and peoples of his age. Yet the Lord Christ says that the lilies of the field, which appear for a day and wither, are more splendidly arrayed than Solomon was in all his glory (Mt 6:29).

9.20.2.en: Moreover, this book did not record Solomon's deviations and his fall, which are recorded in First Kings. Perhaps the Scripture offers us an important lesson, that even if the great and the wise may fall, and their fall is serious, it is not for us to expose them at every time. On the other hand, perhaps Solomon offered repentance for them, and therefore the book is silent about them, because they were forgiven him (Ezek 33:16). God in His love for man no longer remembers our sins as long as we have returned to Him and left the way of evil.

9.20.3.en: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold [13]

9.20.4.en: This weight of gold is equivalent to about 25 tons of gold. Yet the wise man later records for us his experience in the Book of Ecclesiastes: “Vanity of vanities; all is vanity.” And it is written in the Book of Proverbs: “Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith. Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith” (Prov 15:16-17).

9.20.5.en: Most likely she heard from him such words of wisdom while she saw the riches of his palace and the treasures of his storehouses, and so it was said of her: “There was no more spirit in her” [4].

9.21.0.en: Beside that which chapmen and merchants brought.

9.21.1.en: And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon. [14]

9.22.0.en: And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one target [15]

9.22.1.en: God promised Solomon that He would give him riches and honor along with wisdom (2 Chr 1:11-12; 1 Kgs 3:12-13). Riches in themselves are not a sin, for Abraham was very rich, and gave all his wealth to his son Isaac (Gen 24:34-36). The management of wealth is not a sin; rather the love of money is a sin (1 Tim 6:7-10). Solomon himself wrote: “He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity” (Eccl 5:10).

9.23.0.en: And three hundred shields made he of beaten gold: three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield.

9.23.1.en: And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon. [16]

9.24.0.en: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold. [17]

9.25.0.en: And there were six steps to the throne.

9.25.1.en: With a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and stays on each side of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays. [18]

9.25.2.en: The feet of Solomon were placed on pure gold. And it was said of the Lord Christ: [Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne] (Ps 89:14; see Ps 97:2).

9.26.0.en: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps.

9.26.1.en: There was not the like made in any kingdom. [19]

9.26.2.en: Solomon wished to affirm his wealth and power, so he adorned his throne and his house with statues of lions, but the Lord Christ declared His capabilities by granting His disciples and believers authority to tread upon the devil and the powers of darkness, so that they do not fear the lion that walketh about, seeking whom he may devour (1 Pet 5:8).

9.26.3.en: v Do you want to be a virgin?... If you long for all this, overcome the flesh, defeat the lusts of the flesh, overcome the world in the Spirit of God, triumph over the vain temporal things which pass and grow old and corrupt and come to an end, overcome the dragon (Rev 12:7), overcome the lion (1 Pet 5:8), overcome the serpent (2 Cor 11:3), overcome Satan, by Jesus who strengthens you, by your hearing His words and your enjoying the Eucharist in God. Take up His cross and follow Him (Mt 26:24), He who purifies you, Jesus Christ your Lord[10].

9.26.4.en: St. Clement of Rome v After your victories, which flow from His victories, the angels also receive you and glorify you and serve you as guardians for you in everything[11].

9.27.0.en: And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold.

9.27.1.en: None were of silver; it was not any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon [20]

9.27.2.en: Solomon displayed his greatness by using vessels all of gold, but our Christ displays His greatness by raising us, who are of the dust, to be heavenly, for gold signifies heaven.

9.27.3.en: v He was born in a manger, to raise you to the altar; He came to earth, to raise you to heaven; He found no place for Himself except in the manger of the oxen, that He might offer you mansions in heaven (Jn 14:2), and as the Apostle says: “Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich” (2 Cor 9:8). My inheritance is the poverty of Christ, and my strength is the weakness of Christ.

9.27.4.en: St. Ambrose v He feeds those who are counted among men as heavenly, until they reach eternity, setting aside the lusts of the flesh so that they fall shattered[12].

9.28.0.en: For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks. [21]

9.29.0.en: And king Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom. [22]

9.29.1.en: Solomon became great in riches, glory and wisdom, things which God gave him. But for us, our Christ has become riches and satisfaction and wisdom!

9.29.2.en: v Who supports us? Jesus Christ, the Word of God and the Wisdom of God. Moreover He sustains us, not for a day or two, but eternally[13].

9.29.3.en: Origen v He who truly believes is wholly united with Him in whom are truth, divinity, essence, life and wisdom, and sees in Him all these, which are not in him who does not believe. For without the Son of God you have no existence and no name, and the strong becomes without strength, and the wise without wisdom. For Christ is “the power of God, and the wisdom of God” (1 Cor 24:1); he who thinks that he sees the One God without power, without truth, without wisdom, without life and without true light, either sees nothing at all, or certainly sees what is evil[14].

9.30.0.en: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that God had put in his heart. [23]

9.30.1.en: The kings of the earth longed to hear Solomon because of the wisdom God gave him; and the believers, whom the Lord, the King of kings, makes kings, seek His presence in order to possess Him as the Wisdom of God.

9.31.0.en: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year. [24]

9.32.0.en: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; whom he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem. [25]

9.32.1.en: Solomon did not heed the Law's warning to kings: “But he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt, to the end that he should multiply horses” (Deut 17:16).

9.33.0.en: And he reigned over all the kings from the river even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt. [26]

9.33.1.en: And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones,

9.34.0.en: And cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the low plains in abundance. [27]

9.35.0.en: And they brought unto Solomon horses out of Egypt, and out of all lands. [28]

9.36.0.en: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat? [29]

9.37.0.en: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years. [30]

9.37.1.en: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father.

9.38.0.en: And Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead. [31]

9.38.1.en: The book closed its account of Solomon without mentioning his falls in his love for foreign women and his turning aside to the worship of idols through them. This is because his kingdom is a symbol of the Kingdom of Christ, which must be holy and without sin, shining with the splendor of the Sun of Righteousness.

9.38.2.en: Let me meet You and possess You, O Wisdom of God!

9.38.3.en: v The queen of Sheba set out to Solomon, since she had heard of him.

9.38.4.en: And behold, You, the Lord of Solomon, have come down to me.

9.38.5.en: The queen of Sheba heard of the wisdom of Solomon, and carried gifts to him!

9.38.6.en: But You call me to be united with You, and to enjoy the fellowship of Your glory.

9.38.7.en: v Allow me to reveal to You all that is in my heart.

9.38.8.en: By Your Holy Spirit I sit at Your feet.

9.38.9.en: There I commune with You, O Bridegroom of my soul.

9.38.10.en: I hear Your voice, and enjoy Your splendor.

9.38.11.en: My heart melts in love for You.

9.38.12.en: And I long that all humanity be drawn to You.

9.38.13.en: v The queen of Sheba met those who worked in Solomon's palace.

9.38.14.en: She was dazzled by the management of his palace, and blessed those who worked with him and heard him.

9.38.15.en: But You open to me the doors of Your heavens.

9.38.16.en: I bless the prophets and apostles and disciples and all the believers.

9.38.17.en: And I long to praise You with them, as with all the heavenly orders.

9.38.18.en: I see in Paradise thieves who have become saints.

9.38.19.en: And I feel Your grace which has made those of the dust almost heavenly.

9.38.20.en: I stand in amazement before the riches of Your surpassing grace!

9.38.21.en: v The queen of Sheba counted all those around You the happiest of those on earth.

9.38.22.en: And behold, I see Your Church, the unique bride.

9.38.23.en: She bears the reflection of Your splendor, O You who are fairer than the children of men!

9.38.24.en: By Your light You have removed from her all darkness.

9.38.25.en: And by Your grace she has come to bear Your righteousness.

9.38.26.en: By Your cross she has become the queen sitting at Your right hand!

9.38.27.en: v Her dwelling has become with You in heaven.

9.38.28.en: Where the lion who longs to devour her cannot creep in to her!

9.38.29.en: The enemy will find nothing of his in her!

9.38.30.en: You are her light and her glory and her riches and her happiness.

9.38.31.en: You are everything, so she lacks nothing.

9.38.32.en: v Grant me to cling to You and possess You.

9.38.33.en: I will not leave You, but You dwell in me and I in You.

9.38.34.en: To You be glory, O power of God and wisdom of God.

9.38.35.en: In You I experience the earnest of Your heavens.

9.38.36.en: In You my heart and my mind are lifted up as to heaven.

9.38.37.en: In You I live happily whatever troubles of the world may come!

9.38.38.en: You lift me from glory to glory!
